question: Identify the Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who constructed a new garrison town named Siri for his soldiers.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khalji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alauddin Khalji was the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in India.
 
• He reigned from 1296 to 1316 AD.
 
• He constructed the city of Siri in 1303 AD to serve as a military garrison and administrative center.
 
• Siri Fort, a part of this new city, was built to protect Delhi from Mongol invasions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**

 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent for 320 years (1206–1526).
 
• It was established by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a former slave who became the first Sultan of Delhi.
 
• The Sultanate is known for repelling the Mongol invasions and for its cultural and architectural achievements.
 
 
 
• **Alauddin Khalji's Reforms:**
 
 
• He implemented significant economic and military reforms to strengthen his administration.
 
• Introduced price controls and rationing to ensure food security and prevent hoarding.
 
• Reorganized the army and implemented a system of branding horses to prevent corruption.
 
 
 
• **Siri:**
 
 
• Siri was the second city of Delhi built by Alauddin Khalji, known for its strategic and military importance.
 
• The city included the Siri Fort, which served as a defensive structure against invasions.
 
• Siri was noted for its architectural innovations and contributed to the urban development of Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Mongol Invasions:**
 
 
• During Alauddin Khalji's reign, the Delhi Sultanate faced repeated invasions from the Mongols.
 
• He successfully repelled these invasions through military prowess and strategic fortifications.
 
• The construction of Siri was part of his efforts to protect the Sultanate from external threats.
